jobs.title: Director, Corporate FP&A
jobs.description:
About Monster Energy:

Forget about blending in. That's not our style. We're the risk takers, the trailblazers, the gamechangers. We're not perfect and we don't pretend to be. We're raw, unfiltered, and a bit unconventional. Our drive is just like our athletes, unrivaled. The power is in your hands to define what success looks like and where you want to take your career. It's not just about what we do, but about who we become on along the way. We are much more than a brand here. We are a way of life, a mindset. Join us.

A Day in the Life:

The Director, Corporate FP&A will lead Monster Energy corporate financial planning (budgeting, forecasting, analysis). In partnership with the Principal, Corporate Development & FP&A , this role will also support execution of financial M&A integration work, technical accounting analysis, and other corporate strategic initiatives. The Director, Corporate FP&A will be a critical partner across various internal teams and as such, should provide a high level of customer service to Monster Energy employees across all departments and levels.

The Impact You'll Make:

- Provide primary ownership over all forward-looking financial projections and budgeting related to Monster Energy management company

- Partner with the executive management team to facilitate strategic planning and analysis. Run and manage multiple scenarios that reflect the most recent same store business plan, capital markets transactions and/or acquisitions.

- Continuously improve systems, business processes, and reporting capabilities of the Corporate FP&A team using BPC/SAP SAC system.

- Assume overall responsibility for the completeness, accuracy and integrity of source data used in budgets, reforecasts, and internal management reports

- Optimize and/or implement relevant processes to gather, analyze and store benchmarking metrics, ensuring necessary tools are in place to drive business decision making. Includes providing ongoing, relevant public company competitor set benchmarking and analyses of the alternative asset management industry

- Coordinate with Investments, Capital Markets, and Finance Leadership to ensure that recurring and ad-hoc analyses prepared by FP&A meets the needs of all stakeholders and is delivered accurately, efficiently, and timely.

- Assist Investments teams with transaction support work (including corporate M&A, new investments, and/or financing for the management company). Provide support for due diligence and other related requests, as needed.

- In partnership with relevant teams, support execution of M&A integration work. Specifically, manage implementation of business process initiatives to ensure the accuracy, reliability and efficiency of the accounting, budgeting and forecasting processes. Identify opportunities for cost reductions and synergies throughout the company, as part of integration efforts

- Provide analyses of NPV and monitor payback of internal initiatives. Includes ongoing project support to a) enable forward progress on initiatives, and b) ensure economics remain on track/aligned to business outcomes

- Apply knowledge of US GAAP and fair-value GAAP to ensure fair-value adjustments are appropriately layered into cash flow actual results and projections on a consistent basis

- Additional projects, as assigned

Who You Are:

- Bachelor's degree in accounting, Finance or related field

- 10+ years of relevant professional experience in FP&A

- Demonstrated experience providing technical accounting guidance on complex transactions, business combinations, revenue recognition, etc. required.

- Prior asset and investment management business experience a plus (incl. corporate aspects of alternative asset management)

- Investment banking, private equity or management consulting industry experience preferred

- CPA, CFA, MBA preferred

- Experience with public company benchmarking and analyses of the alternative asset management industry a plus

- 3+ years of Big 4 or other public accounting experience preferred, specifically Transaction Services

- 4+ years of hands-on leadership experience within finance and accounting functions

- Highest level of technical expertise in SAP SAC, BW, BI, Microsoft Office: Excel, Word, Access & PowerPoint

- Complex financial modeling experience required

- Exceptional to technical with US GAAP required; IFRS and/or other GAAP basis a plus

- Programming experience with SQL, Excel Macros (VBA) or other similar languages (optional)

- Experience with Adaptive Planning, SAP SAC/FP&A Planning, or similar forecasting software preferred

Monster Energy provides competitive total compensation. The estimated annual salary range for this position is listed below. Actual compensation may vary based on skills, qualifications, experience, and work location.

Pay Range
$154,500 — $206,000 USD

For United States applicants:

jobs.title: Vice President, Commercial Strategy and Planning
jobs.description:
About Monster Energy:

Forget about blending in. That's not our style. We're the risk takers, the trailblazers, the gamechangers. We're not perfect and we don't pretend to be. We're raw, unfiltered, and a bit unconventional. Our drive is just like our athletes, unrivaled. The power is in your hands to define what success looks like and where you want to take your career. It's not just about what we do, but about who we become on along the way. We are much more than a brand here. We are a way of life, a mindset. Join us.

A Day in the Life:

As Vice President, Commercial Strategy & Planning, you will be a key leader in driving Monter Energy's North America growth strategy. You will lead the development and execution of commercial strategies across customer segments, channels, and markets to deliver sustainable, profitable growth.

In this role, you will own end-to-end commercial planning, including go-to-market strategies, portfolio priorities, distribution expansion, and investment recommendations. Working collaboratively across Commercial, Operations, Finance, and Marketing, you will ensure alignment between strategy and execution, helping Monter Energy capitalize on emerging opportunities, respond to market trends, and achieve its long-term growth objectives.

The Impact You'll Make:

- Develop the North America 3–5 year commercial growth architecture to ensure the business is structured for scale.

- Lead the commercial planning processes - including sources of growth, innovation, channel planning, go-to-market planning, and distribution expansion; direct the go-to-market planning process across channels, customer segments, and geographies to achieve our annual and long-range plan targets and ensure adherence to MEC brand objectives.

- Integrate eCommerce and digital commerce into the commercial planning process, ensuring omnichannel strategy keeps pace with evolving shopper behavior.

- Define the strategic customer framework and joint business planning standards that guide how Monster Energy invests in and grows its most critical retail and foodservice relationships.

- Lead product lifecycle management, including retirement strategies and exit plans, to reduce complexity and drive consistent execution on the most productive items across the system; execute new product commercial readiness and launch execution standards to improve innovation speed to market and reduce execution risk.

- Partner cross-functionally with Sales, Finance, Marketing, and Supply Chain to ensure commercial strategies and capabilities are fully integrated and operationally executable across the business; align the North America Coca-Cola bottler system to ensure Monster Energy, bottlers, and retailers move in sync.

- Identify and address market opportunities, competitive dynamics, and category trends to sharpen strategic priorities and ensure Monster Energy stays ahead of shifts in the marketplace.

- Lead business case development and investment recommendations for new commercial initiatives, packages, channel expansions, and strategic partnerships to enable confident, data-backed decision-making at the executive level.

- Build, develop, and lead a high-performing team, establishing clear accountability structures and coaching team members to grow their strategic, analytical, and planning capabilities; maintain commercial performance measurement frameworks that give leadership clear, real-time visibility into progress against key growth objectives.

Who You Are:

-  Bachelor's Degree in the field of Business, Strategy, Marketing, or a related field required. MBA or advanced degree strongly preferred.

- More than 10 years of experience in strategic leadership, commercial strategy, go-to-market planning, and business development

- More than 5 years of experience in a senior leadership capacity with demonstrated ability to operate at the executive level
Computer Skills Desired: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. PowerBI reporting experience highly desired.

- Working knowledge of Nielsen and/or IRI syndicated data platforms.

- Strong command of commercial planning processes and financial modeling tools.

- Proven experience developing and executing commercial strategies in a consumer goods, beverage, or high-growth consumer brand environment

- Track record of preparing and presenting to C-suite leaders, boards, and external stakeholders.

- Experience leading cross-functional teams and managing complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives in a matrixed organization.

A day in the life:

As the Procurement Manager - Commodities, you will be responsible for managing the day-to-day sourcing and procurement of all commodity ingredients and supporting leadership on all global initiatives. Implement and maintain the global procurement and supply plan to fit with the company's strategies and growth in all regions. Work with all regional procurement managers to ensure the company is receiving the best value and pricing while ensuring supply continuity.

The impact you'll make:

- Understand and monitor all current supply agreements and their respective timing for renewal. Lead negotiations and execution of new, renewed agreements regarding supply terms, costing and commercial terms of all key commodity ingredient suppliers.

- Assess and approve commodity market details. Devise ways and means to maximize commodity buying efficiency and minimize risks. Develop and manage pricing strategies. Draft proposals to manage contracts and negotiations.

- Responsible for helping to ensure a robust, reliable and sustainable supply chain for all commodity ingredients globally, so that the supply chain is never broken, customers are served right, and revenue is never missed.

- Helping to implement the global sourcing and supply strategy with critical segmentation of suppliers (strategic, tactical, opportunistic). Helping to implement strong contingencies around critical sourcing areas. The major focus will be in North America with limited support to other regions.

- Help to implement the Core Procurement Processes to comply with the company's financial requirements and expectations 'Protect the Brand.'

- Strong focus on managing inflationary pressures and cost savings through detailed planning and execution of productivity ideas and projects. Help to conduct external and internal assessments of the competitive landscape, suppliers and market trends, work with internal teams to identify opportunities to drive program growth.

- Work with suppliers, cross-functional partners and key stakeholders to ensure communication of project updates and changes to the supply chain. Respond timely to supplier and costing requirements from stakeholders globally.

- Ensure all suppliers are aligned with Monster's Quality Assurance /Quality Control processes and procedures. Supports regional and global supply and quality issues; actively participates in the resolution of crisis level issues.

- Assist accounting in resolving price discrepancies.

Who you are:

- Prefer a Bachelor's Degree in the field of -- Business Administration, Supply Chain, Finance, Analytics or related field.
